rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read, all 4 chunks. Chunk 0 L9 'the commit your un-packaged run started at' and L7 'the session you sent off from' resolve under the session-artifact carve-out (the student's own M4 send-off). L11 'the first run' is continuation of L9 within the same chunk. Chunk 1 L21 'the second session' vs 'the first' reuses chunk 0's term. L22's 'Module 1', 'Module 4', 'Module 6' are bare module-name references, explicitly listed as NOT a violation ('module names'). Chunk 2 L33 'The output' is immediate continuation of chunk 1's prompt-run subject; L35 'the two paths Claude checked' names CLAUDE.local.md/observations/ two lines earlier in the same chunk. Chunk 3 L39 'the m4/<slug> branch', 'the Run coordinates block', '"M4 starting point" commit' are arc-earned vocabulary established in M4's own exercise (verified: `grep -n "Run coordinates\|M4 starting point" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` -> L162 names both, produced via `exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` § Pin the starting point, a prior module in this training's arc). L40 'the send-off' reuses chunk 0's own term. L41 'the branch you cut it from' addresses the student's own repo state (session-artifact class), not a missing system referent. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

No chunk points at another file's content by position. `./task.md` (L39) and file paths in the prompt block are named, real artifacts the student's own session holds -- navigational, not narrative callback, per the §2 carve-out. Module references (L22) name modules by number, not by relative position ('the previous module'). Closest candidate: L39 'Claude normally reads the protected Run coordinates block in task.md' -- passes because the file is named directly, not located ('the file from before').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked each backward reference against the module's current file set. 'M4 starting point' / 'Run coordinates' (L39-40): confirmed live in `curriculum/exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` (M4, per `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` L162, prompt `ae101-m4-commit-starting-point`) -- the beat exists. 'what you built in Module 1 and Module 4' (L22): CLAUDE.local.md and observations/ are both live artifacts of those modules per `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/training-architecture.md` and `getting-going.md`/`run-the-first-experiment.md`. 'After Module 6 you decide what to merge back' (L22, forward-referencing beat): `curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` and its module both exist and cover exactly the merge-back decision. No dead beat.

Every ## chunk carries a self-standing, multi-bullet claim: chunk 1 (4 bullets + prompt) explains what runs in the worktree and why gitignored files need copying; chunk 2 (3 bullets) is the copy-verification check; chunk 3 (3 bullets) is the coordinate-recovery ladder. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Covered each header, then checked the body against it. 'Phase 1: Fork it' (L17) -> body forks the worktree and copies gitignored files, all forking-scoped. 'Check the copy landed' (L31) -> body is exactly output/manual-verify/extra-paths checks. 'Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (L37) -> body is the run-coordinates recovery ladder; the maintainer's own accept-note (L55) confirms the neutral heading is deliberate because the first bullet is the primary path, not a fallback label.

Checked each sub-item across all 4 chunks. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triple. No self-grading superlative -- closest is L13 'The point: a worktree lets you run the same task twice as a split test', a factual mechanism claim, not a value-prop judgement about the exercise's own worth. No number-with-retraction hedge (L21 'diagnosis, verifier, reference, plan.md, and the re-send' and L33 'two variables instead of one' are fixed factual counts, never walked back). No abstraction-noun stack -- nouns throughout are concrete (worktree, commit, branch, SHA, CLAUDE.local.md, observations/). No verb triplet with an empty leg.

'un-packaged'/'packaged' (L9, L21) are AE101's own taught arc vocabulary (the module's own title is 'Learn from the test, re-send packaged'), not maintainer-internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 carries 5 bolded spans (Time:, Session, What you do:, What you build:, The point:) but these are the exercise-opener template's own mandated field labels, not narrative bold: confirmed against `curriculum/widgets.md` L11 ('**Session** *(verb, "name")*' is the fixed widget syntax the renderer keys on) and `curriculum/exercises/README.md` (`**What you do:**`/`**What you build:**`/`**The point:**` are the prescribed exercise-header shape, used identically across every exercise file, e.g. `author-test-strategy-skill.md` L7-11). Same logic as the compendium's own module-LO-bullet exception: the template mandates the bold, not the author -- N/A per the rule's own instruction to check whether a template requires the spend before charging a count violation. Chunks 1-3 carry zero narrative bold (only the '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' widget label, itself template-mandated) -- well inside the <=1 budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an exercise file: all three ## headings are imperative or phase-label, not declarative claims -- 'Phase 1: Fork it' (phase label + imperative verb), 'Check the copy landed' (imperative), 'Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (imperative). No law/consolidation-style declarative heading is present, so the claim requirement is not in play here and none was needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every bullet against the three classes. None is doctrine restatement: L21 names concrete artefacts (diagnosis, verifier, reference, plan.md, re-send), not a re-announced split/lens; L33 'A rules file that didn't copy changes two variables instead of one, and the contrast stops meaning anything' states a concrete new failure consequence, not a repeat of L13's split-test line. None is self-referential design commentary (no 'this is by design' / pedagogy-naming line anywhere in the body). None is an aphorism kicker restating its own header or the **The point:** line -- L13's **The point:** is the widget-mandated opener field itself, not echoed by any later bullet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Trigger check: `git diff 0cea7581..HEAD -- curriculum/exercises/fork-the-worktree.md` touches no `##` line at all -- 'Phase 1: Fork it' is unchanged since well before the pin. The maintainer's own provenance note (L59, dated 2026-08-25, predating the pin) describes content MOVED IN under this existing, unrenamed header, not a rename left with stale bullets: covering the header and reading only the body, the two new opening bullets (why the work runs in a worktree, why gitignored files need the copy) both answer 'Fork it' directly. No rename event in scope; body matches its header.
